result: CONFIRMED by exact installed Lean4.33.1/Lake source inspection; no build was run
findings: reportJob classifies a logged warning in any nonoptional job as a failure, without a root-package/dependency-package test.
Module fetch replays saved traces even for up-to-date/cached compiled modules, so prebuilding dependencies does not by itself make --wfail warning-free.
Printing options such as --quiet do not change failure classification and must not be used as a workaround.

LeanLib.leanOptions composes each library own package options; adding warningAsError=true only to Hironaka package enforces local Hironaka warnings as errors without changing the DeJongAlterations package configuration.
Lean built-in warningAsError converts logged warning severity into an error; it does not suppress warning messages.
recommendation: Set Hironaka [leanOptions] warningAsError=true and use/document ordinary lake build for the integrated default. Keep all upstream linter options and logs intact; inventory their warning modules/counts. This preserves fatal-warning discipline for Hironaka own modules and leaves dependency warnings visible. If literal global lake build --wfail must remain the success criterion, genuinely repair upstream warnings and pin that newly checked source revision instead.
